headline: Medium-risk shared-network pair: no direct injection or filesystem conflict, but broad egress and file-upload surfaces create leakage and cascading-error exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Neither profile shows a shared filesystem or clipboard bridge, so direct injection is not default. However, Plane accepts file uploads and EMQX exposes an HTTP API with broad egress, so if operators manually pass content between them, Plane content could be treated as instructions by EMQX workflows. This is a manual-bridge risk, not a default one.
conditions: IF operators copy Plane-uploaded content into EMQX-managed workflows, injection becomes plausible.
IF a shared workspace or clipboard is introduced, the risk increases.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Do not paste Plane file contents into EMQX control inputs.
Add a human review step before any EMQX action triggered from Plane text.
requires-engineering: add provenance labels to transferred content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Plane can ingest file uploads and EMQX touches IoT data; both have broad network egress. Even without a shared filesystem, any operator-mediated transfer of uploaded files or IoT payloads between them can leak sensitive content to the other agent's backend or outputs. The pairwise pathway exists in common workflows, so this is more than low risk.
conditions: IF Plane file uploads contain sensitive project data and are forwarded to EMQX, leakage occurs.
IF EMQX IoT payloads are copied into Plane notes or issues, they become broadly accessible there.
mitigations: Restrict uploads in Plane to non-sensitive files.
Redact IoT payloads before copying into Plane.
Use separate accounts and workspaces.
Review outbound integrations on both systems.
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on file uploads and exports.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: EMQX has HTTP API access, while Plane supports file uploads and multiple instances, but Plane explicitly lacks filesystem write and neither profile shows overlapping write access to the same mutable resource. That makes direct capability conflict unlikely. Uncertainty is limited because the profiles do not expose shared write surfaces.
conditions: IF both agents are later granted write access to the same directory or database, conflicts become plausible.
IF an orchestrator adds shared mutable state, contention risk increases.
mitigations: Keep write scopes disjoint.
Avoid shared mutable folders.
Run each agent under separate service accounts.
requires-engineering: add locking around any shared resource.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Plane can store issues, tasks, and notes, so it can easily become the downstream consumer of EMQX-generated text. EMQX has broad egress and an HTTP API, so if its outputs are treated as authoritative by Plane workflows, errors can cascade into tickets or plans without verification. The pathway is plausible in default operational use, though not proven by direct evidence.
conditions: IF Plane automations ingest EMQX output without review, erroneous actions can propagate.
IF EMQX-generated summaries are copied into issues or roadmaps, downstream decisions may rely on them.
mitigations: Require human review before creating Plane issues from EMQX output.
Mark EMQX-derived text as untrusted in Plane.
Limit automation to draft-only status.
Add source links to every imported item.
requires-engineering: implement verification checks before actioning outputs.

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented in either profile, and both are open-source with docs-only evidence. The only compliance-relevant clue is that Plane handles files and EMQX touches IoT data, but there is no direct indication of regulated data classes or conflicting policies. This remains a low-confidence, low-severity compliance gap.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in Plane file uploads, policy review is required.
IF EMQX processes jurisdiction-bound IoT data, residency controls must be checked.
mitigations: Classify data before use.
Avoid placing regulated data in either system.
Review retention settings in Plane.
Review deployment region for EMQX.
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls.
